title: A sheaf whose finite direct image on a curve is constructible is constructible
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $X$ and $Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$ of dimension at most one, let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ whose direct image $f_*F$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is torsion, so that $(X,F)$ and $(Y,f_*F)$ are curve coefficient pairs [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. If $f_*F$ is constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion], then $F$ is constructible.

source.place: Etale Cohomology: the converse of Lemma 095R (lemma-finite-pushforward-constructible), needed for the assertions (4), (5) of Lemma 0A5D ('those statements that apply', Section 03SB, list after Situation 03SB) for f_*F. Intended proof: the counit f^{-1}f_*F -> F is surjective (on stalks it is the projection of the finite stalk formula, lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula, onto the factor of the given point), f^{-1}f_*F is constructible (Lemma 095G, lemma-pullback-constructible), and a quotient of a constructible abelian sheaf on a Noetherian scheme is constructible (Proposition 09BH, proposition-constructible-over-noetherian (2)). Not stated in Stacks; the composition of these three is the agent's.

proof.text: *Notation; $X$ and $Y$ are Noetherian.* Write $G=f_*F$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], a torsion sheaf on $Y_{\Et}$ by hypothesis, and $F'=f^{-1}G=f^{-1}f_*F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], with counit $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_{f,F}:F'\to F$ of the adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$. $X$ and $Y$ are of finite type over the field $k$, hence Noetherian schemes, and their underlying spaces are Noetherian topological spaces; so every locally closed subset of $X$ is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset] (Stacks Topology 005L, recorded there). Since $X$ is separated of finite type over the algebraically closed $k$ with $\dim X\le1$, a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ makes a curve coefficient pair with $X$ [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting].

source.place: Section 'Constructible sheaves on Noetherian schemes' (section-noetherian-constructible), first paragraph: on a Noetherian scheme locally closed strata are automatically constructible.

proof.text: *The counit is surjective on every geometric stalk.* Let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] and $\bar y=f\circ\bar x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-counit-stalk-germ-restriction], $\varepsilon_{\bar x}=r_{f,\bar x,F}\circ c_{f,\bar x,G}$, where $c_{f,\bar x,G}:F'_{\bar x}\to G_{\bar y}$ is the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] and $r_{f,\bar x,F}:G_{\bar y}=(f_*F)_{\bar y}\to F_{\bar x}$ is the restriction of germs. As $f$ is finite, $\bar x$ belongs to the finite set $P(\bar y)$ of geometric points of $X$ over $\bar y$ with field $\Omega$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction] the map $(r_{f,\bar x',F})_{\bar x'\in P(\bar y)}:(f_*F)_{\bar y}\to\prod_{\bar x'\in P(\bar y)}F_{\bar x'}$ is an isomorphism (the finite stalk formula [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] with its components named). So $r_{f,\bar x,F}$ is this isomorphism followed by the projection onto the factor $\bar x$, which is surjective; composed with the isomorphism $c_{f,\bar x,G}$, $\varepsilon_{\bar x}$ is surjective.

source.place: Proposition 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero) (1) and its proof, with Lemma 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback); the identification of the counit on stalks with the projection is the agent's (cf. the proof of Lemma 0959, lemma-finite-pushforward-commutes-with-base-change, which computes a pullback map on stalks the same way).

proof.text: *The counit is an epimorphism.* Let $Q=\operatorname{Coker}\varepsilon$ in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For every point $x\in X$ choose a geometric point $\bar x$ over it (Spec of an algebraic closure of $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-geometric-point]); these geometric points cover $X$. Stalk functors are exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], so $Q_{\bar x}=\operatorname{Coker}(\varepsilon_{\bar x})=0$ by step 2. Hence the morphism $Q\to0$ is injective on the stalks of a covering family of geometric points, so it is a monomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-detect-mono], i.e. $Q=0$; in the abelian category $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ a morphism with zero cokernel is an epimorphism. With $K=\operatorname{Ker}\varepsilon\subseteq F'$ and $\kappa:K\to F'$ the inclusion, $0\to K\xrightarrow{\kappa}F'\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}F\to0$ is a short exact sequence in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$.

source.place: Theorem 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks): exactness is checked on stalks at geometric points; here via the covering-family form of the reviewed sibling lem-weil-pbc-curve-constructible-sub-quotient, step 1(d).

proof.text: *$F'=f^{-1}f_*F$ is constructible (Stacks 095G for abelian sheaves).* By [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion] for the curve coefficient pair $(Y,G)$ there are a finite partition $Y=\coprod_{i=1}^rY_i$ into locally closed constructible subsets and immersions $u_i:Z_i\to Y$ with image $Y_i$ such that $u_i^{-1}G$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is locally constant [def-constructible-locally-constant] with finite geometric stalks. Let $Z_i'=Z_i\times_YX$ with projections $u_i':Z_i'\to X$ and $f_i:Z_i'\to Z_i$, so $f\circ u_i'=u_i\circ f_i$. (a) *The strata.* By [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification] the $u_i'$ are immersions forming a stratification of $X$ [def-constructible-stratification] with strata $X_i=f^{-1}(Y_i)$: pairwise disjoint locally closed subsets covering $X$. Each $X_i$ is constructible, $X$ being Noetherian (step 1). So $(u_i':Z_i'\to X)_i$ is a finite partition of $X$ into locally closed constructible subschemes. (b) *Local constancy.* By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2), applied to $(f,u_i')$ and to $(u_i,f_i)$, there are isomorphisms $u_i'^{-1}F'=u_i'^{-1}f^{-1}G\cong(f\circ u_i')^{-1}G=(u_i\circ f_i)^{-1}G\cong f_i^{-1}(u_i^{-1}G)$. The sheaf $f_i^{-1}(u_i^{-1}G)$ is locally constant by [lemma-constructible-pullback-locally-constant] (coefficients: abelian groups), hence so is $u_i'^{-1}F'$ by [lemma-constructible-iso-invariance]. (c) *Finite stalks.* For a geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z_i'$, $(u_i'^{-1}F')_{\bar z}\cong(f_i^{-1}u_i^{-1}G)_{\bar z}\cong(u_i^{-1}G)_{f_i\circ\bar z}$ [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar], a stalk of $u_i^{-1}G$ at the geometric point $f_i\circ\bar z$ of $Z_i$ (same algebraically closed field), which is finite. (d) $F'$ is torsion: for every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, $F'_{\bar x}\cong G_{f\circ\bar x}$ [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] is a torsion group since $G$ is torsion ((1)$\Rightarrow$(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations]), so $F'$ is torsion by (3)$\Rightarrow$(1),(2) there, and $(X,F')$ is a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. By (a)-(c), $F'$ is constructible in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion].

source.place: Lemma 095G (lemma-pullback-constructible) and its proof: 'we just pull back the partition of Y adapted to F and use Lemma 095A (lemma-pullback-locally-constant)'; the reduction to affines there (Lemmas 09BE, 095E) is not needed for the global partition form on the Noetherian X.

proof.text: *$K$ is torsion.* $\kappa$ is a monomorphism, so for every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ the map $\kappa_{\bar x}:K_{\bar x}\to F'_{\bar x}$ is injective [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]; $F'_{\bar x}$ is torsion (step 4 (d)), hence so is its subgroup $K_{\bar x}$, and $K$ is torsion by (3)$\Rightarrow$(1),(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations]. So $(X,K)$, $(X,F')$, $(X,F)$ are curve coefficient pairs [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] ($F$ is torsion by hypothesis).

source.place: Section 0DDB (section-torsion, 'Torsion sheaves'): a subsheaf of a torsion sheaf is torsion; written out here (agent).

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-curve-constructible-sub-quotient] on $C=X$ to the short exact sequence $0\to K\to F'\to F\to0$ of step 3, whose three terms are torsion (step 5) and whose middle term $F'$ is constructible in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion] (step 4): the quotient $F$ is constructible in the same sense.

source.place: Proposition 09BH (proposition-constructible-over-noetherian) (2): a quotient of a constructible abelian sheaf on a Noetherian scheme is constructible.

proof_origin.place: The composition is not in Stacks (the converse of Lemma 095R, lemma-finite-pushforward-constructible); it combines Proposition 03QP (1) (finite stalk formula), Lemma 095G (pullback of constructible), Theorem 03PU (exactness on stalks) and Proposition 09BH (2) (quotients of constructible sheaves on Noetherian schemes); the identification of the counit on stalks is written out by the agent.

Proof in six steps along the intended route of the source field: (1) notation, X Noetherian (elementary); (2) the counit f^{-1}f_*F -> F is surjective on every geometric stalk: its stalk is the restriction of germs r composed with the inverse-image stalk iso (new node lem-weil-pbc-counit-stalk-germ-restriction, any morphism; Lean slopmaster2 Etale.stalkRestrict_eq_counit, sorry-free), and for finite f the r's over a geometric point assemble to the finite stalk formula iso (new node lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction, the explicit form of the closed lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula; Lean Etale.isIso_piLift_stalkRestrict, sorry-free); (3) epimorphism: cokernel zero on a covering family of stalks, via prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact and the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-detect-mono (as in the sibling); (4) f^{-1}f_*F constructible in the curve sense, following Stacks 095G's proof directly in the curve sense with the closed nodes lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification, lemma-constructible-pullback-locally-constant, lemma-constructible-iso-invariance, lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar and lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition (strata constructible because X is Noetherian), plus torsion via lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations; prop-constructible-pullback (closed) was not cited directly because its finiteness clause (def-constructible-finite) quantifies over separably closed geometric points while the curve definition uses algebraically closed ones; (5) the kernel is torsion; (6) the reviewed sibling lem-weil-pbc-curve-constructible-sub-quotient (Stacks 09BH (2)) gives F constructible as the quotient.
